recipes.name: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice
ingredients_raw: 1 pound andouille sausage, sliced into rounds
1 medium jalapeno pepper, seeded and chopped
1 pound dried red beans, soaked overnight
1 teaspoon Creole seasoning, or to taste

steps.text: Brown sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat, 5 to 7 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer sausage to a slow cooker, leaving drippings in the skillet.
Add onion, bell pepper, jalapeño, and garlic to drippings in the skillet; cook and stir over medium heat until tender, about 5 minutes. Transfer to the slow cooker.
Add soaked beans and ham hock to the slow cooker, then pour in water. Add basil, Creole seasoning, and pepper. Cover and cook on Low until beans are tender, about 8 hours.
If the bean mixture is too watery, remove the lid, increase the heat to High, and cook until beans are creamy. Serve with cooked rice.

raw_recipe.headline: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice
raw_recipe.description: Easy red beans in the crockpot to serve over rice! Just simmer the beans with sausage, a ham hock, peppers, and some seasoning — and check back in 8 hours!

review.reviewBody: This is the best recipe for red beans & rice on this site. It does need tweaking for your individual tastes, though. To make these red beans taste like the ones I grew up on in Louisiana, I did the following: Omitted the jalapeño. Cut the bell pepper by half. Used a generous amount of Tony Chachere's cajun seasoning. Subbed chicken broth for water & cut it down to 7 cups. Used the back of my spoon to smash up enough beans to make the whole pot creamy. Must! Use! Andouille! even if you have to order it online this is the ONLY way to get the authentic and unique flavor of the sausage right. Regular sausage just isn't seasoned the same way or contains the same amount of spiciness. My central Texas grocery store has started carrying it, as does Whole Foods and other "specialty stores". I only had ham scraps instead of a ham hock but the andouille adds smoky flavor so I didn't miss the hock. Normally I'd use both the andouille & the ham hock. For those omitting celery, you really need the "holy trinity" of onion, celery & bell pepper to call it authentic. Mince it finely and sautee it first if you have to. Me, I just do a fine dice on the veggies and let them cook down in the pot.

In N'awlins, everybody has her own touch for red beans and rice, so whatever works for you is great. They are ALL creamy, though, accomplished by smashing beans as noted by several folks. Most restaurants serve smoked sausage on the side and season the beans with ham or a little andouille. One tip--don't add the salt until the end or it will prevent the beans from getting soft.

I’m giving 4 stars because I made quite a few changes to the recipe. I didn’t have all of the ingredients so I made some substitutions. First off did a quick soak on ½ a package of small red beans (followed the directions on the bag). In a dutch oven I browned 1 lb Portuguese smoked sausage (doubled the sausage since I didn’t have the ham hock). I then set the sausage aside and sautéed 1 diced yellow onion, 1 diced red bell pepper,1 diced yellow bell pepper, and 6 cloves of garlic. Then to the veggies I added, black pepper, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, thyme, and Creole seasoning. I also added chicken stock granules and beef stock granules. Continued to cook the veggies with spices till tender then added 5 cups of water, beans, cooked sausage and 2 bay leaves, let it simmer and tilted the lid and let it simmer for about 3 hours till the liquid was absorbed and beans were soft. Mixed with cooked long grain rice. I cut the beans, rice and water in half since its just me and I don’t want to eat red beans and rice for a week but left the rest of the ingredients the same measurements if not more and added more seasonings since a lot of the reviews suggested it. I had also planned to make it the crock pot but ran out of time and went with my trusty cast iron Dutch oven, worked Great! Will def make again.

Don't use 10 cups of water. Insanity. 7 cups is plenty. Fresh basil because bay leaves because it is more authentic. (I had to skim about 4 cups of water off my beans... 2 cups went into the pot to make the rice). Mashed up some beans to help the consistency and voila! Perfect beans. Varied the spices to my taste. Have made this 2x and I love it. Freezes well.

I am making it for the second time today. Just about the best I have ever made the first time around. Too much water in the recipe so I cut it down to 8 cups this time. I put some green onions in the mix. I didn't use the creole seasoning mix but rather used individual seasonings of my choice so I wouldn't get the salt. Crock pot cooking works great for this dish.

Another touch I do is remove the ham hock towards the end, cut away the fat, and chop up the ham hock meat to add back to the pot. I suggest adding a bay leaf and about a teaspoon of cumin. Cumin is a great seasoning for bean dishes.

If you happen to wake up and find you didn't soak your beans overnight it is not really necessary for this recipe. The long cooking time in the crock pot will get the beans tender. If you must, a couple of hours soaking in the morning will work too.

Great flavor but the recipe needs some tweaking. Otherwise, I would have given it 5 stars. So simple to put together. Ten cups of liquid is WAY too much, though. It was pretty soupy even after I mashed some of the beans. I had to add corn starch to thicken it up and then let it cook with the lid off for a couple hours longer than the recipe says to get it to the right consistency. Next time, I'd go with about 6 cups of liquid instead of 10. I used chicken stock instead of water which gave it a really nice flavor. I would definitely make this again, just with a few changes.

this was very savory but i prepared it differently after reading many other recipes. after placing the soaked beans and 2 small hamhocks in the pot i added enough water to cover the beans plus 1 inch. i also added a cube of mexican chicken bouillion, i tsp liquid smoke and 1/4 cup miced garlic. i added everything to the pot but the andouille sausage and cooked on low for 6hrs. i removed the ham hocks, mashed 1/3 of the beans with a potato masher,then added back the hock meat and sliced andouille to cook for 2 hours so it wouldn't get all shriveled up. HTH

We loved this recipe! Made it exactly as directed but had to sub another sausage (jalapeno/chicken) for the andouille and using beef broth for half the water. This makes such a hearty, flavorful dish for minimal effort. I did find it to have way too much liquid and next time I would cut back on the liquid to 7-8 cups. I pureed some of the beans to thicken it slightly and give it some body. The flavor is awesome, thanks Melissa!

My wife was from near to New Iberia, La. We ate red beans and rice on a regular basis. She liked to coarse chop some jalapeno pepper along with the bell pepper, onion and a little celery. She parboiled the slices of sausage to remove some of the grease before adding. When the beans were softened, she mashed about a third of them to give a gravy-like consistency. Sometimes she added a little rough chopped tasso or partially fried sliced salt pork to enhance the flavor. Everyone (including me) loved her beans. She also cooked dried white beans in a similar fashion and they were spectacular!

This is really a pretty good recipe. I adjusted the spices to suit my families taste, and made a couple of substitutions due to location and price. I subbed hot sausage (from Hillshire Farms) for the andouille sausage, and I used ham boullion instead of a ham hock. My only thing is that in the slow cooker the thing would not thicken- so I ended up pouring it into a pan and simmering for about 20 minutes to reduce the liquid. Next time I'll just use less liquid- probably more like 7-8 cups of water. Over all though it is a really tasty recipe that is pretty forgiving when it comes to adjusting here and there for your own taste.

This was delicious. I didn't use any ham hock and I added the sausage near the end. I substituted 7 cups of chicken broth instead of 10 cups of water. This was still too much liquid. I'll try 5.5 cups next time. Also, I left out the jalapeno (only because I didn't have one) and I used Tony's and some extra red pepper. Also, I mashed some of the red beans to make it a bit creamier. Like I said, it was delicious. I don't know if I've found my perfect recipe, but maybe with some more tiny tweeks it will get there.

I used 7 cups chicken stock, 1 lbs thick smoked bacon instead of ham hocks, and smashed beans at end of cook. Otherwise followed the recipe. Came out creamy. It tasted really good. The only red beans and rice I've had was from Popeyes. This is just as good. I'll add celery next time.

10 cups of water? Step 5: "If the bean mixture is too watery, remove the lid, increase the heat to High, and cook until beans are creamy." Yeah, right! I used 9 cups; checked at 7 hours and 40 minutes or so and decided to take off the lid and turn to high. That didn't help the extra water so i moved out of crock pot into pan on stove to boil it down. Not sure it will be dinner at this rate. And what drippings? smoked andouille was all that was available, so i had to add olive oil to cook it and saute the veggies. not impressed.
This did not come out creamy and I only used 6 cups of water. I would reduce it to 4. My finished result is very watery :(

First time to make this. I followed a few of the suggestions from Kay. Used chicken broth, but will cut it to 6 cups next time. I mashed some of the beans, but feel it was still too liquid. I added the celery and jalapeno and used andouille sausage. I also added the ham hock. We liked it and will make again with my changes.
Absolutely s keeper my family said to make this weekly
When the beans are soft, I put about three cups in the food processor. Then add them back in for another hour. Very creamy. Also add Louisiana hot sauce to taste.
It's an excellent recipe. The only thing I did differently was add 1/2 cup red wine vinegar. It does bring out the different flavors and gives them a zing. I'd make this again and again!

It's good, but definitely missing something. I can't quite put my finger on it. My picky eaters (husband and son) still enjoyed it though, as did I. I just needs something...extra Also, I added celery
